chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the condition in female slaves that they should not be sold, nor inherited, nor gifted. He said: 'That is permissible, except for inheritance, for she is inherited, because every condition that contradicts the Book is void.'

Ibn Sinan said: And I asked him about a slave who has partners, and one of them sold his share. One of them said: 'I have more right to it.' Is that so? He said: 'Yes, if he is one (i.e., if there are only two partners).'.

key_terms.الشَّرْط: Condition or stipulation attached to a contract

ai.seo_question: What are the valid conditions for selling and inheriting female slaves in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle that contractual conditions are valid unless they explicitly contradict the Quran, using inheritance as the primary example of an immutable divine law. It further elucidates the jurisprudence of pre-emption (*shuf'ah*) among co-owners, restricting this priority right to cases of exactly two partners, a nuance significant in Shia commercial law for resolving disputes over shared assets.
